entry.title: [UPDATED] RUSTSEC-2026-0384: Race condition in `tokio::time::Interval` on Tokio v1.54.0
entry.content:
Race condition in `tokio::time::Interval` on Tokio v1.54.0

Aliases: CVE-2026-115567, GHSA-5wjr-9356-4wc8

Affected:

  • tokio — fixed in 1.54.1

## Summary On the multi-threaded runtime, there is a race condition between `Interval::poll_tick` and the runtime's time driver. This affects `Interval` only. `Sleep` and `Timeout` are **not** affected. ## Details In Tokio v1.54.0, a race condition between `tokio::time::Interval::poll_tick` (including `.tick().await`) and the runtime time driver can drop an internal timer entry without synchronizing with the driver thread that is firing it. This causes a data race and use-after-free on the timer's waker and task state in safe Rust, leading to assertion panics, task reference-count corruption, or heap memory corruption. This bug was introduced by https://github.com/tokio-rs/tokio/pull/8458, and it was fixed by https://github.com/tokio-rs/tokio/pull/8692. ## Impact This may lead to cr…

entry.title: [NEW] RUSTSEC-2026-0387: Multiple timing variability issues in operations intended to be constant-time
entry.content:
Multiple timing variability issues in operations intended to be constant-time

Affected:

  • crypto-bigint — fixed in 0.7.6

## Summary Several operations intended to be constant-time could execute secret-dependent branches, depending on the compiler and target CPU. These include subtraction, zero counting, division, and Montgomery multiplication. Additionally, `UintRef` equality could terminate at the first unequal limb, and `BoxedMontyForm::invert` branched on whether an inverse exists. ## Impact Applications using affected operations on secret integers may leak information through timing or microarchitectural side channels. This includes information about intermediate arithmetic values, matching limbs, and invertibility. Such leakage could potentially enable recovery of cryptographic secrets. Practical exploitability depends on the downstream algorithm, compiler, target CPU, and an attacker's ability to …

entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-897f-g5gm-fmxm: Wasmtime: Bit-packing in Cranelift compiler causes silent overflow and miscompilation
entry.content:
Wasmtime: Bit-packing in Cranelift compiler causes silent overflow and miscompilation

Aliases: CVE-2026-115889, RUSTSEC-2026-0380

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H

Affected:

  • wasmtime — fixed in 36.0.19
  • wasmtime — fixed in 43.0.0

## Summary In Wasmtime prior to v43, the Cranelift compiler backend bit-packs its SSA value indices in a way that can result in silent overflow in release builds, and result in incorrect value references in the IR resulting in arbitrary miscompilation. A very large Wasm function body, or one that is specially crafted to use many SSA values, can use this to force type-confusion or other arbitrary side-effects and escape the sandbox. Cranelift was changed in Wasmtime v43 to use a full `u32` index, with checks if that limit is exceeded, and so is no longer susceptible to this bug. ## Impact A Wasmtime engine with default settings (using the Cranelift backend) on any architecture/platform could experience a sandbox escape from a specially-crafted Wasm module. ## Patches Wasmtime v36.0.19…

entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-h4fr-cmh5-qr62: Fallow: A `.*` glob segment let an analyzed repository make Fallow test paths in the parent of the project root
entry.content:
Fallow: A `.*` glob segment let an analyzed repository make Fallow test paths in the parent of the project root

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N

Affected:

  • fallow — fixed in 3.34.0
  • @fallow-cli/fallow-node — fixed in 3.34.0
  • fallow-cli — fixed in 3.34.0
  • fallow-config — fixed in 3.34.0

entry.title: [UPDATED] RUSTSEC-2026-0386: `AsyncFd::new` and related constructors violate I/O safety
entry.content:
`AsyncFd::new` and related constructors violate I/O safety

Affected:

  • tokio — fixed in 1.51.6, 1.53.3

`tokio::io::unix::AsyncFd` provides safe constructors (`new`, `with_interest`, `try_new`, and `try_with_interest`) that accept any `T: AsRawFd` rather than requiring proof of ownership or validity of the file descriptor. Because `RawFd` implements `AsRawFd`, safe code can construct an `AsyncFd` from an arbitrary or closed file descriptor, or close/replace the underlying file descriptor while the `AsyncFd` is still alive. This violates I/O safety in two ways: 1. `AsyncFd<T>` implements `AsFd` for all `T: AsRawFd` by calling `BorrowedFd::borrow_raw(self.as_raw_fd())`, allowing safe code to obtain an arbitrary `BorrowedFd<'_>` without owning the file descriptor. 2. Tokio's I/O driver stores a pointer to an internal allocation in the `epoll`/`kqueue` user data for registered file descriptors…

entry.title: [UPDATED] RUSTSEC-2026-0305: Use-after-free when XML includes have duplicated entities
entry.content:
Use-after-free when XML includes have duplicated entities

Aliases: CVE-2026-96889, GHSA-cpvr-w4j5-2mpg

Affected:

  • librsvg — fixed in 2.57.5, 2.60.3, 2.61.5, 2.62.4, 2.63.2

Librsvg uses libxml2, a C library, to parse XML. When librsvg parses an SVG document which has a nested Xinclude, an XML entity declaration with a duplicate name as an existing one can cause a use-after-free error. While libxml2 is expanding an internal entity, a recursive XInclude can parse another document that declares an entity with the same name. Both parses use the same `XmlState` entity map on the librsvg side. `entity_insert()` replaces the first entry, whose `Drop` implementation calls `xmlFreeNode()`. The outer `xmlCtxtParseEntity()` then keeps using the freed 144-byte `xmlEntity`. The included parse should not free an entity that the outer parser is still using. The fix is in commit 8a1b0cd319e9af2d1e9cf878081dd77f227a0504, where librsvg will no longer free xmlEntity pointer…
